channel.title: California Uzbek — Latest
channel.description: Independent analysis · Central Asia & world geopolitics

item.title: How to manage and get out of debt: the avalanche and snowball methods
item.description: High-interest debt — a credit card or consumer loan — can grow fast and strangle a family for years. This neutral reference explains, on the basis of sources, the two main repayment methods — the avalanche and the snowball — the minimum-payment trap, and where to get legitimate free help. It is not financial advice.

item.title: Number of Uzbeks going abroad to study fell 33% in nine months
item.description: In January–September 2026, 16,522 citizens travelled abroad for study. Russia overtook Tajikistan as the most popular destination.

item.title: Kazakh women break the silence under #IAmJaneDoe
item.description: Thousands of women are speaking out about childhood sexual violence. A law exists — but gaps remain.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea: diplomatic ties and the Daewoo investment (1992–1996)
item.description: In the first years of independence, South Korea became one of Uzbekistan's most important economic partners. Diplomatic ties established in 1992 and the automobile joint venture with Daewoo — the Asaka plant in Andijan — laid the foundation for the first large-scale car manufacturing in Central Asia. This neutral history recounts that period on the basis of sources, with verified facts only.

item.title: Uzbekistan offers eligible AI projects up to 10mn free tokens a month
item.description: Under a 20 October Cabinet resolution, startups, universities and research organisations can use the state AI infrastructure free or at a discount for up to six months.

item.title: In November, seniors get 50% off museums and heritage sites and 20% off rail
item.description: During the 1–30 November 'Tourism Month for the Elderly,' pensioners get discounts at heritage sites and museums and on domestic rail and hotels.

item.title: Kazakhstan's new parliament restricts journalists' access to officials
item.description: In the Kurultai, questions are allowed only at scheduled briefings. An off-topic question brings a warning; two violations mean a 6-month loss of accreditation.

item.title: The Turkestan Legion and postwar emigration (1941–1945): from captivity to the Western diaspora
item.description: In World War II, Nazi Germany formed the "Turkestan Legion" from Soviet prisoners of war — Uzbeks, Kazakhs, Turkmens, Kyrgyz and Tajiks. For most it was not ideology but a forced choice to survive starvation. This neutral history, on the basis of sources and verified facts only, recounts the legion's formation, the roles of Veli Kayum Khan and Mustafa Chokay, and how survivors became part of the Western diaspora.

item.title: How AI chatbots work and why they "hallucinate"
item.description: Chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini are not machines that "know" — they are language models that predict the next word by probability. This neutral reference explains, on the basis of sources, how they work, why they sometimes answer with confident falsehoods (hallucination), and how to use them critically.

item.title: The deportation of the North Caucasus peoples to Central Asia (1943–1944): Karachays, Chechens, Ingush and Balkars
item.description: During the Second World War, Stalin's regime deported whole peoples of the North Caucasus — Karachays, Chechens, Ingush and Balkars — in railway wagons to Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and, in part, Uzbekistan. This fact-based historical reference sets out the dates, numbers and the 1957 rehabilitation.

item.title: Germany recruits Uzbek truck drivers: €1,800 monthly after tax
item.description: Uzbekistan's Migration Agency, with German firm RecruitMed, opened a competition for 50 positions, requiring C and CE licences, with six months of free German-language training and online interviews on 6 and 10 November.

item.title: Online security basics: strong passwords, two-step protection and avoiding phishing
item.description: A neutral, source-based guide to protecting your accounts and personal data online: how to build a password, why two-factor authentication matters, how to recognize phishing (scam messages), and what to do if you are hacked. This is not technical or legal advice.

item.title: Nodir Jonuzoq: state-language use in agencies was below 50% seven years ago, now fully in Uzbek
item.description: The head of the state-language development department told the 'Oydin Gurunglar 2026' forum that 5,292 geographical names have been standardised and the Terminology Commission approved nearly 100 terms after a 30-year pause.

item.title: The establishment of Uzbekistan–Russia relations (1991–1996): diplomacy, a treaty and an independent path
item.description: After independence in 1991, how did Uzbekistan build its relationship with its former center, Russia? This fact-based historical reference sets out, with dates, the establishment of diplomatic relations, the 1992 Treaty of Friendship, monetary independence and the emigration of the Russian-speaking population.

item.title: Uzbekistan to screen students and educators psychologically every year — with AI analysing the results
item.description: Under a presidential decree of 19 October, targeted psychological diagnostics will run through an electronic platform; the first phase starts in the 2026/2027 school year in kindergartens and schools.

item.title: Mirziyoyev at Karshi State University: 14,000 students, 7 laboratories and three new dormitories
item.description: The president reviewed facilities at the Kashkadarya university: new dormitories with 1,300 places, artificial-intelligence and robotics laboratories, and a 1,000-capacity media studio.

item.title: New Imkon centre opens in Samarkand: preschool for 150 children and rehabilitation for 100 a month
item.description: The new centre in the National Agency for Social Protection's network combines education and treatment; the network provided over 546,000 treatments in 2025.

item.title: How the U.S. federal government works: the three branches and checks and balances
item.description: A neutral reference for Uzbeks living in the United States: why the Constitution splits power into three branches — legislative, executive and judicial — how they limit one another, and the difference between the federal and state governments. This is not political advice.

item.title: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visits Karshi State University: 14,000 students, 3 new dormitories, 7 laboratories
item.description: According to the Presidential Press Service, the head of state toured the university's internationally accredited programmes, joint degrees and research laboratories during a trip to Kashkadarya.

item.title: How to verify information: lateral reading, the SIFT method and reverse image search
item.description: Checking a claim before you share it is the foundation of media literacy. This practical reference explains the techniques professional fact-checkers use — lateral reading and the SIFT method, reverse image search, and how to judge whether a source is reliable — on the basis of sources.

item.title: The establishment of Uzbekistan–Turkey relations: the first country to recognise it (1991–1996)
item.description: Turkey was the first country in the world to recognise Uzbekistan’s independence. This historical reference sets out the establishment of diplomatic, educational and economic ties between the two states in 1991–1996, with exact dates and facts.

item.title: The four changed letters of the revised Uzbek alphabet: an Uzbek tradition or a Turkic turn?
item.description: The letters Ş, Ç, Ö, Ğ in the revised Uzbek Latin alphabet look Turkic to many. In fact they were already part of the original 1993 alphabet. The arguments and objections around the reform.

item.title: Ohio: after Haitian migrants lost protection, Springfield began to empty out
item.description: After the Trump administration ended Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haitians, Springfield — home to roughly 15,000 migrants — is seeing workers dwindle and some businesses close.

item.title: The 1944 deportation of the Crimean Tatars to Uzbekistan and the making of a community
item.description: In May 1944 the Soviet government deported the entire Crimean Tatar people from their homeland; most were resettled in Uzbekistan. This historical reference sets out the exact dates, figures, consequences and road to rehabilitation on the basis of sources.

item.title: Uzbekistan to play friendly against Saudi Arabia in Doha on November 17
item.description: According to the Uzbekistan Football Association, Fabio Cannavaro's side will face Saudi Arabia in Doha on November 17; a friendly against Russia is also scheduled for November.

item.title: Uzbekistan's annual inflation eased to 6.4% in September, core inflation at 5.5%
item.description: The Central Bank said inflation fell from 8% a year earlier but warned that price pressures persist, keeping monetary policy tight.

item.title: Ziroat Mirziyoyeva named chair of global network supporting seriously ill children
item.description: The initiative was announced in Samarkand at the Second International Congress on Childhood Cancer; Uzbekistan's First Lady will chair the network for two years and received a WHO certificate of recognition.

item.title: How ETFs and index funds work: the basics of passive investing and diversification
item.description: An index fund or exchange-traded fund (ETF) lets a single purchase buy a slice of dozens or hundreds of companies. This neutral reference explains passive investing, diversification, the expense ratio and the risks, on the basis of sources. It is not financial advice.

item.title: Russia steps up expulsions in Novosibirsk: 32 Uzbek citizens removed on October 16
item.description: Expulsions of foreign nationals from the Novosibirsk region rose about 59% in a year; Uzbek citizens make up a large share of those removed for migration violations.

item.title: Top destinations for Uzbek travelers: Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan and Tajikistan lead
item.description: Nearly 5.9 million Uzbek citizens traveled abroad for tourism in January–September 2026, with most choosing three neighboring countries.
